messages:
anna_support: FYI customer EdgeFlick reporting repeated 429s across several regions starting 2024-11-02 08:45 UTC. They say it looks like bursts at top-of-minute.

anna_support: Key bits from their logs: `x-request-id: ef-89234`, `x-rpm: 720`, `x-tpm: 220`, responses: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests` with body `{'error':'rate_limited'}`.

anna_support: They're on hosted plan, making concurrent streaming requests to /v1/chat.stream, client is a server-side worker (Go) with default retry loop. Customer says they didn't change traffic pattern.

sam_eng: thanks anna — can you confirm which endpoint (generation vs chat) and exact region? also do they have multiple API keys / parallel machines?

anna_support: chat streaming - region: us-west-2. Single API key but ~40 worker processes each with up to 10 concurrent streams. So bursts of ~300 concurrent connections for 10s at minute boundary.

marta_sre: that concurrency + minute-boundary alignment screams quota-window exhaustion. If their client tries to align heartbeats/cron at same second we see sawtooth. do we have per-customer RPM/TPM logs for ef-89234?

anna_support: attaching snippet they pasted (sanitized):
```
2024-11-02T08:45:00Z POST /v1/chat.stream 200 12ms tokens=34
2024-11-02T08:45:00Z POST /v1/chat.stream 429 1ms x-request-id=ef-89234
2024-11-02T08:45:01Z POST /v1/chat.stream 429 1ms x-request-id=ef-89235
... repeated ~160 times over 20s window
```

jinja_oncall: +1 to the bucket/window theory. Quick mitigation options: 1) short-term quota bump for EdgeFlick 2) ask them to randomize start times (jitter) 3) enable request smoothing on their tenant if eligible. Which do they want?

edgeflick_ops: thanks team. We can try jittering but it's in prod cron that's tricky. Would prefer a temporary bump while we rollout fix. How fast can that happen?

anna_support: i can request a temporary soft bump from account ops — need expected sustained TPS/RPM number and timeframe. what should we ask for?

sam_eng: before bump, let's verify whether retries are amplifying the spike. ask EdgeFlick for a request-id sample and client retry policy. If they have exponential backoff with zero jitter and immediate retries we could be generating retried bursts that blow through the bucket.

edgeflick_ops: client uses exponential backoff but retries after 100ms initially, 2 attempts max. We've instrumented and see retries concentrated right after 429s.

marta_sre: that explains amplification — each 429 triggers retries that pile into next window. Playbook: 1) temporary quota bump +10-20% for 2 hours 2) advise customer to add jitter and increase base retry to 500ms 3) set support rate-limit rule to allow smoothing if possible 4) collect flamegraph of their request arrivals.

anna_support: submitted internal request to ops for +30% RPM/TMP for 2 hours — ticket #OPS-7321. Ops responded: can apply by EOD but need a pair approval from infra.

sam_eng: meanwhile we should gather data for root cause: - ask them for `X-Request-ID` list + timestamps - enable debug logging for sampling on our proxy for that API key - check `minute_bucket_mismatch` metric and `window_fill_rate` for that tenant.

sam_eng: quick repro steps for eng if you want to test locally:
```
# simulate 40 workers * 8 streams each aligned to minute boundary
for i in {1..320}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat.stream -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d @payload &
done
sleep 30
# observe 429s within next minute
```

jinja_oncall: deploy-bot: note — we just pushed small routing change at 2024-11-02T07:10:00Z but it's unrelated.

deploy-bot: [deploy] service:edge-proxy version:v3.14.2 deployed by:ci/cd pipeline id: 14567 at 2024-11-02T07:10:12Z :white_check_mark:

anna_support: ops approved temporary bump, applied at 2024-11-02T10:05 UTC. customer reports 429s subsided for next 30 minutes.

edgeflick_ops: we rolled jitter and raised initial retry to 600ms. initial results look stable. thanks.

marta_sre: please keep them at +10% for 24h while they monitor. i'll create a Grafana panel to track per-tenant `requests_per_minute`, `throttled_count`, and `avg_queue_wait`. Should help validate fix.

sam_eng: follow-ups for product: consider offering a tenant-level smoothing feature (server-side token bucket smoothing) to avoid customer churn for cron-aligned workloads. filing feature suggestion: PROD-4538.

anna_support: summary for ticket OPS-7321: cause = customer minute-aligned concurrency + retry amplification; mitigation = temporary quota bump + client jitter & retry tuning; next steps = monitor dashboards for 24h, consider product smoothing. closing once metrics stable. :thumbsup:
